correctness.rationale: Independently verified the factorial-moment reduction. For the quadratic part of the benefit, the factorial second moment of K+1 differs from that of the defector's K by 2(n−1)(i−1)(N−n)/[(N−1)(N−2)]; the linear moment difference is (N−n)/(N−1). With the specified cost and coefficient these give the displayed affine payoff gap and then κ(2i−N) exactly on balance. Reflection swaps birth and death probabilities, including at the boundaries where only exploration remains. The chain is irreducible for the stated μ range, with positive stationary weights; the detailed-balance ratios give reflection symmetry and fixed cooperator mean. On each upper-half interior edge for κ>0 the numerator is nondecreasing and the denominator strictly decreasing with w. At i=N−1 it is the numerator that is strictly increasing while the denominator is fixed. This includes N=3 (only the boundary comparison), even N (the zero-gap center still has a strict denominator), and odd N (the central edge joins identical deviations). The signs reverse when κ<0, and rates are constant in w for κ=0. Since folding only multiplies by intensity-independent multiplicities, successive upper-half ratios give all stated strict likelihood-ratio inequalities. Positivity and normalization make each proper upper tail strict: the weighted average of the increasing likelihood ratio on the upper tail is larger than the overall average one. The variance and heterozygosity identities follow by centering.
